title: Binary-Only Schema Upgrades
pattern: Using raw memory layouts, programming-language-specific binary serialization (e.g., Java Serialization, Python pickle, or raw C struct casting), or format-unversioned byte buffers for network communication or long-lived database records.
why_bad: Language-specific binary serialization is fragile. Any refactoring—renaming a variable, changing struct alignment, or adding a field—instantly breaks deserialization, preventing rolling upgrades and making older archived data unreadable [187, 828].
detection: Casting raw byte pointers directly to struct types (`unsafe { &*(bytes.as_ptr() as *const NetworkPayload) }`) or using serialization libraries lacking field tags or structural tolerance.
counterexample: Valid for intra-process communication or ephemeral memory-mapped files where reader and writer are compiled into the exact same binary. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Use versioned, schema-driven binary protocols like Protobuf, Avro, or Thrift, or standard self-describing formats like JSON/MessagePack [187, 829].
source: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, "Assembling a Data Transfer Object" [828]; Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 4, "Programming-language-specific encodings" [187, 653]
